html:
A line of sand berms, ditches and minefields about 2,700 km long, built by Morocco across Western Sahara in six stages between 1980 and 1987.

It walled off the coast, the towns and the Bou Craa phosphate mine, about four fifths of the land, from the raids of the Polisario Front. Radar and troops posted along it made deep raids almost impossible, and the war settled into a stalemate that led to the 1991 ceasefire. Millions of landmines remain around it, and nomad families on both sides are cut off from each other. It is one of the longest military barriers in the world.
sum: A line of sand berms, ditches and minefields about 2,700 km long, built by Morocco across Western Sahara in six stages between 1980 and 1987.
